verdict_rationale: The metric, chance floor and failure handling are sound, the scorer is shipped to the agent, and the gate is self-checked at full size. But the held-out pool mix differs from the shipped validation file in ways the agent is not told, the 'no hand-written rules' line is looser in review than in the prompt, and one SE is about 2 points, enough to tie the $10 winners.
floor: 0 = macro F1 0.5, a fair coin's analytic value on the class-balanced splits (tests/task/task.yaml:38-44, dated 2026-09-26). Always-yes or always-no scores 1/3 (validate.py:10-11), so it clamps to 0. This is a sensible blind baseline. A below-chance classifier also clamps to 0, even when inverting it would score above chance: Muse 57iczy's raw 0.397 would give about 0.60 inverted. The organizer GBDT, length, zero-shot judge and fine-tune baselines exist as code (pipeline/baselines/*.py), but no results are recorded in the repo.
ceiling: 1 = perfect macro F1. Predicting compilation without running Lean makes this unreachable in practice, but it is a natural, non-binding anchor. Best observed: raw 0.7876 (57.9 and 57.5).
feasible_at_10: yes: Sonnet scored 41.8 at $10, and Opus and Astra 37.5 each. A LoRA plus a classification head on an open 7-8B prover fits easily, and CPU Lean labelling costs about $0.14 per core-hour.
budget_scaling: Yes. The 19-model mean rises 17.4 / 19.2 / 22.7, and Opus rises 37.5 / 45.3 / 57.5, with $168 of wallet spent on a 170,600-example self-labelled corpus. More Lean-labelled data and bigger ensembles plausibly buy more. Variance is high: Sonnet scores 41.8 / 31.9 / 57.9.
selfcheck_fidelity: Good for the gates. The self-check runs the no-Lean scan, launches the server as grading does, counts the first request against the budget, and sends a full held-out-sized batch (3,540 distinct copies of public attempts) at concurrency 64 through grading's run_gated, under the same 600 s deadline (tests/task/verifier.py:114-181). File lengths follow the public mix, about half miniF2F, not the held-out mix of Workbook, Pset and FormalMATH variants. A length shift could therefore change throughput (suspected; not measurable without the data). Nothing is scored and the review does not run, so local validation is the only quality signal. Agents that validated on random splits leaking theorems were misled: Muse 57iczy reached 0.9075 locally and 0.397 held-out.
judge: No judge in the metric. The reviewer (Claude Opus 5.5, global) applies five task checks: learned forward pass, no Lean execution or reimplementation, stateless per request, reviewed weights, and training-data provenance with a long miniF2F clause (tests/task/review.py:14-93). The stateless and forward-pass rules can only be enforced by this reviewer reading code.
neutrality: No vendor element. The held-out attempts come from five named open provers: DeepSeek-Prover-V2-7B, Goedel-Prover-V2-8B, Kimina-Prover-Distill-8B, DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-RL and Goedel-Prover-SFT (pipeline/generate.py:19-25). Classifiers started from these same families (the winning recipe used Goedel-Prover-V2-8B) may benefit from familiarity with their own outputs. That is open to every harness and allowed by the non-specialist rule (review.py:78-91). The task rewards knowing the public prover-attempt corpora (Lean-workbook-proofs, Goedel-Pset) whose one-edit variants form the held-out set.
reference_solution: solution/ is the shared smoke fixture. /check always answers {"valid": false} (solution/server.py:76-79). That gives macro F1 1/3, so reward 0, and the fixture cannot pass the learned-model review. No organizer-trained baseline score is recorded. Solvability is shown only by the trials.

issues.finding: There is an undisclosed distribution shift between the shipped file and the held-out set. The validation statements are verbatim public statements: 50% miniF2F-test, 25% Lean Workbook, 25% Goedel-Pset. The held-out statements are numeric or renamed variants drawn 45% Workbook, 45% Pset and 10% FormalMATH, with no miniF2F. SCHEMA.md says the held-out statements are 'private variants of public statements', but not that the pool mix differs. The 526 shipped attempts are the only labelled in-task data, and the prompt says agents may use them for anything. Thresholds calibrated on them transfer poorly: Gemini cnnjfd's curve showed 0.81 on validation, and it scored 0.617 held-out.
evidence: tasks/lean-validity/tests/task/pipeline/build_data.py:76-77 'held-out statements are private variants of public statements (a numeric literal changed and/or variables renamed)'
issues.affects: Every model. It hurts most the agents that leaned on the shipped file for training or threshold choice (DeepSeek 5xiz84, Muse 57iczy and 1xapc5, Gemini cnnjfd). It favours agents that built large Workbook/Pset corpora (Opus).

issues.finding: The reviewer is looser than the prompt on hand-written rules. The prompt says 'the answer has to come from the model, not hand-written rules'. The reviewer only requires that rules 'must not be the source of the prediction', so hand-written validity detectors may feed a learned head. Gemini cnnjfd shipped a blacklist of non-existent Mathlib names and regex detectors as features and passed.

tasks/lean-validity/tests/task/review.py:20-23 'the boolean valid answer is computed from the output of a learned model's forward pass ... hand-written rules or regexes must not be the source of the prediction'
issues.affects: Agents who read the prompt strictly forgo cheap, high-precision features. In the observed runs it won nothing (Gemini 23.4).

issues.finding: The public SCHEMA discloses that every theorem has exactly as many compiling as non-compiling attempts. A server that grouped requests by theorem and forced a 50/50 split within each group would gain a lot. Only the reviewer's stateless check forbids it; no grader mechanism does. All held-out attempts of one theorem share the header and statement text, so grouping is trivial.
evidence: tasks/lean-validity/tests/task/pipeline/build_data.py:58 'every theorem has equally many compiling and non-compiling attempts (3-8 of each)'

tasks/lean-validity/tests/task/review.py:34-38 'No cache, index or statistic built from other evaluation requests (for example grouping attempts of the same theorem, voting, or ranking within a batch) influences a prediction'
issues.affects: No trial exploited it. Enforcement rests entirely on the LLM reviewer.

issues.finding: The noise is larger than the naive binomial value because attempts are clustered: 3,540 attempts on 295 theorems, 12 per theorem. Unclustered, one SE of macro F1 is about 0.007, or 1.4 points after the x2 rescale. With moderate within-theorem correlation it is about 2 points. The $10 winners are 0.04 points apart (Opus 37.55 vs Astra 37.51).
issues.affects: Rankings within about 4 points at a given wallet are not reliable.

issues.finding: The throughput gate is all-or-nothing: all 3,540 answers within 600 s, including the first cold request, or the score is 0. Failed requests score as wrong verdicts, and more than 5% fails the run. The self-check reproduces this at full size, so the fidelity is good, apart from the public-versus-held-out length mix (suspected).
